source: MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, banana cultivation techniques manual, 2019, section VI (harvest, parts 1-2)
text: Timing of harvest is judged mainly by the plumpness and shape of the fingers rather than by skin color alone, since export and market bananas are typically cut while the skin is still green. When the fruit is truly mature but still green, the fingers become rounder and less angular in cross-section, losing the sharp ridges seen on immature fruit; a still-angular, sharply ridged finger with a shiny green peel indicates the fruit is not yet mature enough to cut, even though the color hasn't changed. Farmers are advised to check the roundness of the fingers on a representative bunch (or open one fruit to check the flesh directly) rather than relying on peel color, since color change to yellow is a ripening-stage indicator that typically happens after harvest and during storage/transport, not a harvest-readiness indicator in the field.
